candidates.title: Tune retrieved-document count per aggregation scheme at test time
candidates.rule: Treat the number of retrieved documents as a test-time knob tuned on dev data per decoding scheme: sequence-level marginalisation kept improving with more documents, while token-level marginalisation peaked around 10, so do not copy one setting across variants.
candidates.passage: retrieving more documents at test time monotonically improves Open-domain QA results for RAG-Sequence, but performance peaks for RAG-Token at 10 retrieved documents.
candidates.location: Section 4.5, Effect of Retrieving more documents (Figure 3)
candidates.finding: Models trained with 5 or 10 documents performed similarly, but test-time k mattered differently by variant; final reported settings were 50 documents for RAG-Sequence and 15 for RAG-Token on QA. On MS-MARCO more documents raised Rouge-L but lowered Bleu-1 for RAG-Token, so the metric choice affects the optimum.
models: RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token built on BART-large plus DPR
candidates.conditions: Top-k retrieval from a 21M-passage Wikipedia FAISS index; greedy decoding for QA, beam size 4 for generation; k selected on dev data.
candidates.limitations: Observed in one paper on two tasks with 2020 models; larger k increases latency and compute, and the monotone trend for RAG-Sequence was only shown over the tested range; does not transfer automatically to long-context LLM pipelines.
candidates.validation_test: Sweep k (e.g. 1, 5, 10, 25, 50) at test time for each aggregation strategy on a dev split, record accuracy and per-query latency, and pick k per variant and per target metric.

reason: The paper contains several controlled comparisons (dense DPR vs BM25 retrieval per task; frozen vs fine-tuned query encoder; number of retrieved documents at test time for RAG-Sequence vs RAG-Token) that support narrowly scoped, actionable retrieval-harness rules. Other content (SOTA scores, human preference results) is descriptive rather than a decision rule.
